capsuleTopic.subtitle: Weeks · waiting · wind-like sound · fire-like tongues · languages · witness · widening gift
capsuleTopic.orientation: Begin with the counted Feast of Weeks, then enter Acts 2 as a bounded event: the day arrives, a gathered group is filled, an international crowd hears, Peter interprets, hearers respond, and a new communal life becomes visible. Later receptions remain distinct scenes rather than copies forced into one order.
capsuleTopic.trailPrompt: Follow appointed time, promise, waiting, what is seen and heard, Peter’s speech, response, community, witness, widening reception, and later memory without turning the whole Spirit concept into Pentecost.

passages.title: The Spirit rests on elders and Moses voices a wider wish
passages.excerpt: Moses went out, and told the people the LORD’s words; and he gathered seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them around the Tent. The LORD came down in the cloud, and spoke t…

passages.title: Desolation changes when the Spirit is poured from on high

passages.title: Water and Spirit are promised to thirsty land and offspring

passages.observation: Joel speaks of sons, daughters, elders, youths, servants, wonders, the day of the LORD, and deliverance for those who call on the LORD’s name.

passages.title: David speaks of presence, hope, and not being left in Sheol

passages.title: The LORD addresses David’s Lord at his right hand
passages.excerpt: The LORD says to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool for your feet.”
passages.observation: A short enthronement saying places David’s Lord at the LORD’s right hand until enemies become a footstool.

passages.title: A poured Spirit accompanies looking and mourning

passages.title: John distinguishes water from Spirit-and-fire baptism

passages.title: Expectation turns toward the one who baptizes in Spirit and fire

passages.title: Jesus speaks of the Father giving the Holy Spirit
passages.excerpt: “I tell you, keep asking, and it will be given you. Keep seeking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and it will be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To…
passages.observation: Asking, seeking, knocking, parent-child examples, and the contrast between human and heavenly giving culminate in the Father giving the Holy Spirit to those who ask.

passages.title: Living-water language is explained as the Spirit not yet given

passages.observation: On the feast’s last day Jesus invites the thirsty to drink; the narrator explains the river saying as the Spirit believers were to receive after Jesus was glorified.

passages.title: The Counselor’s testimony and the disciples’ testimony stand together

passages.title: Departure is joined to the Counselor’s coming and guiding

passages.title: The risen Jesus breathes and says, “Receive the Holy Spirit”
passages.excerpt: When therefore it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were locked where the disciples were assembled, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in th…
passages.observation: Jesus appears in a locked room, speaks peace, shows his wounds, commissions the disciples, breathes on them, names the Holy Spirit, and speaks about forgiveness.

passages.title: Witnesses are told to wait in the city for power

passages.title: The apostles are told that Spirit baptism is days away

passages.title: Power, witness, ascension, and united prayer precede the day
passages.excerpt: Therefore, when they had come together, they asked him, “Lord, are you now restoring the kingdom to Israel?” He said to them, “It isn’t for you to know times or seasons which the Father…
passages.observation: Jesus redirects a kingdom-time question toward Spirit-given power and widening witness, ascends, and the apostles return to Jerusalem for persistent shared prayer with the women and Jesus’ family.

passages.title: Matthias is numbered with the Eleven before the day arrives
passages.excerpt: In these days, Peter stood up in the middle of the disciples (and the number of names was about one hundred twenty), and said, “Brothers, it was necessary that this Scripture should be…

passages.title: Sound, divided fire-like tongues, and other languages fill the gathering
passages.excerpt: Now when the day of Pentecost had come, they were all with one accord in one place. Suddenly there came from the sky a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind, and it filled all the hou…
passages.observation: When Pentecost arrives, a heaven-sent sound fills the house, divided tongues like fire rest on each person, all are filled with the Holy Spirit, and they speak other languages.

passages.title: Pilgrims from many regions hear God’s works in their own languages

passages.title: Peter answers mockery by reading the moment through Joel

passages.title: Peter moves from Jesus’ death and resurrection to the visible outpouring

passages.observation: Peter addresses Israel, names Jesus’ works, crucifixion, resurrection, Davidic Scripture, exaltation, the Father’s promise, and the outpouring the crowd sees and hears.

passages.title: The hearers ask, respond, are baptized, and are added

passages.title: Teaching, fellowship, meals, prayers, signs, and shared goods mark the community

passages.observation: Those added continue in apostolic teaching and fellowship, break bread, pray, share property according to need, gather at the temple and homes, and are joined by others.

passages.title: A man at the temple gate walks and praises God

passages.observation: Peter and John meet a man unable to walk, give what they have in Jesus’ name, lift him, and enter the temple with him walking, leaping, and praising.

passages.title: Peter redirects wonder toward Jesus, repentance, and restoration

passages.title: Peter is filled with the Spirit before rulers and elders

passages.observation: Questioned about power and name, Peter speaks while filled with the Holy Spirit, identifies Jesus as crucified and raised, cites the rejected stone, and names salvation.

passages.title: Prayer ends in shaking, filling, and bold speech

passages.observation: The released apostles report the threats, the community prays through creation and Psalm 2, asks for boldness and signs, and the gathered place shakes as all are filled with the Holy Spirit.

passages.title: One heart, apostolic witness, and shared property continue

passages.observation: The believers are one in heart and soul, hold possessions for common use, hear resurrection witness with power, and distribute proceeds according to need.

passages.title: A deceptive gift brings death and great fear
passages.excerpt: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession, and kept back part of the price, his wife also being aware of it, then brought a certain part and laid it at…
passages.observation: Ananias and Sapphira sell property, hold back part of the proceeds while presenting the gift as whole, answer Peter separately, fall dead, and are buried as great fear comes on the assembly.

passages.title: Signs draw crowds from Jerusalem and surrounding towns

passages.observation: Many signs occur through the apostles, believers gather in Solomon’s porch, people are added, and the sick and tormented are brought from neighboring cities.

passages.title: A complaint leads to Spirit-and-wisdom service

passages.title: Stephen sees glory and prays while being killed

passages.observation: Full of the Holy Spirit, Stephen sees Jesus at God’s right hand, while the crowd stops its ears, stones him, and hears his prayers for reception and forgiveness.

passages.title: Samaritans receive the Holy Spirit after receiving the word

passages.observation: Scattered believers preach, Philip’s signs bring joy in Samaria, people are baptized, and Peter and John come from Jerusalem, pray, and lay hands so they receive the Holy Spirit.

passages.title: Simon offers money for apostolic authority and is rebuked

passages.observation: Seeing the Spirit given through the apostles’ hands, Simon offers money for the same authority; Peter rebukes his attempted purchase and heart, Simon asks for prayer, and the apostles return while preaching in Samaritan villages.

passages.title: Saul is filled, baptized, begins preaching, and joins a growing assembly

passages.title: The Spirit falls on Gentile hearers before water baptism

passages.title: Peter calls the Gentile gift what happened “at the beginning”

passages.title: The Spirit names and sends Barnabas and Saul

passages.title: Peter recalls God giving Gentiles the Spirit without distinction

passages.title: Ephesian disciples receive the Spirit, speak languages, and prophesy

passages.observation: Paul asks disciples about receiving the Holy Spirit, explains John’s baptism and Jesus, baptizes them, lays hands on them, and they speak languages and prophesy.

passages.title: Paul hastens toward Jerusalem for Pentecost

passages.title: Paul plans to remain at Ephesus until Pentecost
passages.excerpt: I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia. But with you it may be that I will stay with you, or even winter with you, that you may send…

passages.title: God’s love is described as poured through the given Holy Spirit
passages.excerpt: Being therefore justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ; through whom we also have our access by faith into this grace in which we stand. We rejoice in…
passages.observation: Paul moves through justification, peace, access, suffering, endurance, character, hope, and love poured into hearts through the Holy Spirit given to believers.

passages.title: Many gifts and members are joined by one Spirit

passages.title: Paul asks how the Galatians received the Spirit

passages.title: Hearers who believe are sealed with the promised Holy Spirit

passages.title: The Spirit is said to be poured richly through Jesus Christ
